strategyDescription: A model reads all PR titles and designs 10 discriminating yes/no questions; models answer all questions per PR (batches of 5, title plus 250-char URL-stripped body excerpt) giving a 10-bit signature; TypeScript groups identical signatures and merges groups by average Hamming distance <= 1; groups of 2+ become clusters (named by one call each), singletons and all-false signatures are unclassified. 21 model calls.
noveltyRationale: Evidence representation is a corpus-specific binary question signature designed by a model from the whole title list, not free keywords, closed facet vocabularies, TF-IDF vectors, seeds, pairwise judgments, or recursive splits. Distance is Hamming over shared answers.
validation: 45 PRs: all covered exactly once, known numbers, unique cluster IDs, ranking and window verified independently

lessonsForNextRun: run_rig worked first time; node scripts via create+bash worked while python, heredocs and chained commands were denied.
Question set quality drives everything: the questions mirror the title list, so 10 questions gave 11 clusters, 3 unclassified; threshold 1 was lenient enough to merge near-identical signatures.
Bot-generated PR families (samples, header, claude) cluster cleanly; the provider-integration cluster mixes distinct concerns. No measured comparison to other strategies.
